quizName: DMV Practice Test #2 16 Questions • Passing Score 12

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:

options.text: School crossing sign.
Railroad crossing sign.
Stop sign.
Speed limit sign.

questions.explanation: Speed limit signs are rectangular with white backgrounds and black letters. They tell drivers what rules to follow. Most regulatory signs have this shape and color.

questions.question: Unlike most food and drinks, alcohol does not need to be digested. This means:

options.text: Within minutes of being consumed, the alcohol reaches the brain and begins to affect the drinker.
The alcohol never gets removed from the body.
It takes a long time to feel the effects of alcohol.
Once it is in your system, your body gets rid of the alcohol quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Within minutes of being consumed, the alcohol reaches the brain and begins to affect the drinker.
questions.explanation: Alcohol enters your bloodstream quickly because it does not need to be digested. It reaches your brain within minutes. Your body removes about one drink per hour.

questions.question: The single most important thing you can do to survive a crash is to:

options.text: Wear a high-quality helmet that is securely fastened.
Wear shorts.
Wear sneakers.
Wear goggles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear a high-quality helmet that is securely fastened.
questions.explanation: Wearing a high-quality helmet that is securely fastened is the most effective way to improve your chances of surviving a crash.

questions.question: Before every ride, it is important to check all of the following, except:

options.text: The spokes.
The tire tread.
The lights.
The seat fabric.

questions.explanation: Before every ride, check your spokes for bends or damage, the tire tread condition, and all lights. You do not need to check the seat fabric.

questions.question: When riding, goggles:

options.text: Protect your eyes, but not the rest of your face.
Protect your face, but not your eyes.
Are not as effective at protecting your eyes as eyeglasses.
Are not effective in providing any protection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protect your eyes, but not the rest of your face.
questions.explanation: Goggles protect your eyes. Only a face shield protects your entire face. Eyeglasses do not provide adequate protection.

questions.question: Which of the following surfaces does not provide poor traction?

options.text: Wet pavement
Dry pavement
Lane markings
Snow

questions.explanation: Wet pavement, loose gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, and painted lane markings all have poor traction. Dry pavement provides good traction.

questions.question: If you are riding on the right side of your lane while following a car:

options.text: You are likely riding in the best position to be seen.
You may not be seen unless the driver uses their side mirror.
The driver will most likely assume you are there.
You are discouraging other drivers from sharing your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may not be seen unless the driver uses their side mirror.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of the lane so the driver can see you in their rearview mirror. Drivers check their rearview mirrors more often than their side mirrors.

questions.question: Can clothing help prevent injuries in a crash?

options.text: No, clothing is not really for protection.
No, clothing is more of a personal choice.
Yes, but only if garments are very loose and flap in the wind.
Yes, if pants and a jacket cover your arms and legs completely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, if pants and a jacket cover your arms and legs completely.
questions.explanation: Proper clothing reduces injury risk in a crash. Wear a jacket and pants that cover your arms and legs, are made of sturdy material, and fit snugly so they do not flap.

questions.question: Which of the following is not important when choosing a motorcycle helmet?

options.text: The helmet meets U.S. Department of Transportation standards.
The helmet fits snugly all the way around your head.
The helmet has no obvious defects, such as cracks or loose padding.
The helmet looks cool.

questions.explanation: Check that a helmet meets U.S. DOT standards, fits snugly around your head, and has no cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps. How it looks is not important for protection.

questions.question: Which types of brakes do most motorcycles have?

options.text: Front and emergency
Rear and emergency
Front and rear
Only a front brake

questions.explanation: Most motorcycles have one brake for each wheel. The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake.

questions.question: When riding at night, what is most important?

options.text: You should avoid riding at night.
Wear reflective clothing to be more visible.
Night riding is not safe because drivers cannot see your signals.
Only ride at night in cities.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear reflective clothing to be more visible.
questions.explanation: Wear reflective clothing when riding at night. This makes other drivers able to see you.

questions.question: Most motorcycles have:

options.text: Only a front brake.
Only a rear brake.
Brakes on both the front and rear wheels.
Three brakes: front, rear, and an emergency brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brakes on both the front and rear wheels.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycles have two brakes. One brake controls the front wheel and one controls the rear wheel.

questions.question: How can you help other drivers see your motorcycle?

options.text: Ride with your headlight off.
Wear bright clothing.
Follow other vehicles very closely.
Do not use your turn signals.

questions.explanation: To be seen better, wear bright colored clothing. Also keep your headlight on at all times and always use your turn signals.

questions.question: Before riding your motorcycle, check all of the following except:

options.text: The headlight works.
The oil level.
Both brakes work and the brake light turns on.
The paint is not scratched.

questions.explanation: Before riding, check your tires, oil, and all fluids. Make sure your headlight, taillight, signal lights, and brake light all work. Paint condition is not a safety check.

questions.question: Which of these does NOT protect a motorcycle rider?

options.text: A leather jacket
Boots that cover your ankles
A snug-fitting baseball cap
Gloves

questions.explanation: Wear a DOT-approved helmet, eye protection, a sturdy jacket and long pants, ankle-covering boots, and durable gloves. A baseball cap does not protect you.

questions.question: When riding in traffic, what should you remember about motorcycle blind spots?

options.text: Motorcycles are too small to have blind spots.
Blind spots are too small to be a problem.
You must turn your head to check blind spots.
Motorcycles have only one blind spot.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must turn your head to check blind spots.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like all vehicles. Always turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes.
